key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual, discovered incidentally or with mild symptoms. LOCATION: Headache if present (frontal or occipital). DURATION: Ongoing, chronic. CHARACTER: Asymptomatic or mild headache. AGGRAVATING: Medication non-compliance, stress, salt intake. RELIEVING: Blood pressure reduction. TIMING: Chronic, stable. SEVERITY: Minimal symptoms despite elevated BP. KEY POSITIVES: Elevated BP (>180/120) WITHOUT end-organ damage, asymptomatic or mild headache only, chronic hypertension history. KEY NEGATIVES: NO chest pain, NO altered mental status, NO vision changes, NO dyspnea (those are hypertensive EMERGENCY).
